summary:
Mission Architect is an interactive, web-based space simulation game that empowers users to design, launch, and fly their own space missions. We developed this platform to gamify the complex aerospace engineering process, allowing players—either solo or in teams of up to four—to select missions, build spacecraft, and experience real-time flight telemetry, including Max-Q, stage separation, and orbital execution.

To address the challenge, we directly integrated authentic NASA science into our core gameplay loop. Our spacecraft design phases strictly follow NASA JPL’s Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4), and our underlying mechanics are inspired by GMAT, NASA Eyes, and CubeSat 101.

This project is important because it bridges the critical gap between high-level space science and public accessibility. By transforming the steep learning curve of orbital mechanics into an engaging, hands-on gaming experience, Mission Architect serves as a powerful educational tool designed to inspire the next generation of aerospace engineers and scientists.
details:
How it Works: MISSION ARCHITECT is a browser-based aerospace simulation game built around a three-stage core loop: "Design it, Launch it, Fly it." Players can participate solo or in a local co-op crew of up to 4 players. The experience begins in the design phase, where players conceptualize a mission using frameworks based directly on NASA JPL's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4). Once the spacecraft is approved via the simulated Mission Design Lab, players enter the live flight phase. Here, they monitor a real-time telemetry dashboard tracking Mission Elapsed Time (MET), altitude, velocity, and thrust as they progress through realistic launch stages (Ignition, Liftoff, Max-Q, Stage Separation, and Orbit).

Benefits & Impact: Space mission design is traditionally locked behind complex software with high learning curves. Our project bridges this gap by democratizing aerospace science. The intended impact is highly educational: by gamifying orbital mechanics and spacecraft design, we provide a hands-on, accessible learning tool that inspires students and space enthusiasts without sacrificing scientific authenticity.

Tools & Technologies: Our team of four developed the application natively for the modern web. We utilized HTML5 and the Canvas API for real-time graphics and physics rendering. The UI/UX was custom-designed to mimic authentic aerospace control panels, utilizing web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) to handle dynamic state changes, user inputs, and live telemetry updates.

Creativity & Factors Considered: Our creativity lies in transforming dry, technical protocols into an engaging game. Rather than building a pure science fiction game, we focused heavily on scientific accuracy, integrating concepts from NASA tools like GMAT and CubeSat 101. We carefully considered the balance between realistic engineering constraints and enjoyable gameplay, ensuring the mechanics were intuitive enough for beginners but accurate enough to be genuinely educational.
